newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index touches new 1997 high.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index touches new 1997 high.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars, rose 0.4 percent to reach a new 1997 high of 314.10 at the start of play on Tuesday.
Latin America edged up 0.4 percent day-on-day to 591.52, Asia was up 0.7 percent at 262.48, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were flat at 143.42.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was at a new high, rising 0.38 percent day-on-day to 171.22 at 1100 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index was at a new high level, climbing 0.45 percent to 508.674, calculated after the close of trade on Monday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index, its returns calculated in dollar terms, fell 0.07 percent to 125.84 by the start of trade on Tuesday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996. It reached a 1997 high of 125.93 after the close of trade on 16 January.
By region, Latin America was down 0.07 percent at 103.91, Asia fell 0.03 to 132.55 and East Europe was down 0.39 at 162.28. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
